| $y$ | $9$ | $7$ | $5$ | $3$ |

Consider the data sets above. You are given that $\overset{―}{x}=4$ and $\overset{―}{y}=6.$ Find the equation of the corresponding linear regression line. Round the slope and the $y$-intercept to **one decimal place** if necessary.

$y=$
{{field-1}}
q-316581.worked_solution:
The equation of the regression line is given by

$$
y=mx+b,
$$

where 

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{S}_{xy}}{{S}_{xx}},\,b=\overset{―}{y}-m\overset{―}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's compute $m:$

- First, we compute the sum in the numerator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xy} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & =(1-4)(9-6)+(3-4)(7-6) \\  & +(5-4)(5-6)+(7-4)(3-6) \\  & =(-3)(3)+(-1)(1)+(1)(-1)+(3)(-3) \\  & =-9-1-1-9 \\  & =-20\end{aligned}
$$

- Second, we compute the sum in the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xx} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =(1-4)^{2}+(3-4)^{2}+(5-4)^{2}+(7-4)^{2} \\  & =9+1+1+9 \\  & =20\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting into the formula for $m,$ we obtain 

$$
m=\frac{-20}{20}=-1.
$$

Next, we substitute into the formula for $b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}b & =\overset{―}{y}-m\overset{―}{x} \\  & =6-(-1)\cdot 4 \\  & =6+4 \\  & =10\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the regression line is

$$
y=-x+10.
$$

The table above gives the value of a motorcycle a few years after it was purchased (in thousands of dollars). You are given that x―=2 and y―=16. Find the equation of the corresponding linear regression line and use this to predict how long it takes for the motorcycle to have a value of $8000. Round the answer to the nearest year.

10 years
b
5 years
c
8 years
d
2 years
e
6 years

EXPLANATION

The equation of the regression line is given by

y=mx+b,

where

m=SxySxx,b=y―−mx―.

Let's compute m:

  • First, we compute the sum in the numerator: Sxy=∑i=1n(xi−x―)(yi−y―)=(0−2)(20−16)+(1−2)(18−16)=+(3−2)(15−16)+(4−2)(11−16)=(−2)(4)+(−1)(2)+(1)(−1)+(2)(−5)=−8−2−1−10=−21

  • Second, we compute the sum in the denominator: Sxx=∑i=1n(xi−x―)2=(0−2)2+(1−2)2+(3−2)2+(4−2)2=4+1+1+4=10

Now, substituting into the formula for m, we obtain

m=−2110=−2.1.

Next, we substitute into the formula for b:

b=y―−mx―=16−(−2.1)⋅2=20.2

Therefore, the equation of the regression line is

y=−2.1x+20.2

Finally, we can estimate the required value by substituting y=8 into the equation of the trend line and solving for x:

y=−2.1x+20.28=−2.1x+20.2−12.2=−2.1xx≈6

Therefore, according to this model, it takes 6 years for the motorcycle to have a value of $8000.

Note: Since we're extrapolating (the point where y=8 is not within the original data range), our result may be unreliable.

The table above gives the ages, in years, and the corresponding heights, in centimeters, of Milly and Rasheed's four children. You are given that $\overset{―}{x}=6$ and $\overset{―}{y}=109.$ 

Find the equation of the corresponding linear regression line and use this to predict the children's height when they are $6$ years old. Round the regression line's coefficients to three decimal places and your final answer to the nearest tenth of a centimeter.
q-134208.worked_solution:
The equation of the regression line is given by

$$
y=mx+b,
$$

where 

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{S}_{xy}}{{S}_{xx}},\,b=\overset{―}{y}-m\overset{―}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's compute $m:$

- First, we compute the sum in the numerator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xy} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & =(3-6)(95-109)+(5-6)(106-109) \\  & +(7-6)(110-109)+(9-6)(125-109) \\  & =(-3)(-14)+(-1)(-3)+(1)(1)+(3)(16) \\  & =42+3+1+48 \\  & =94\end{aligned}
$$

- Second, we compute the sum in the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xx} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =(3-6)^{2}+(5-6)^{2}+(7-6)^{2}+(9-6)^{2} \\  & =9+1+1+9 \\  & =20\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting into the formula for $m,$ we obtain 

$$
m=\frac{94}{20}=\frac{47}{10}=4.7.
$$

Next, we substitute into the formula for $b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}b & =\overset{―}{y}-m\overset{―}{x} \\  & =109-4.7\cdot 6 \\  & =109-28.2 \\  & =80.8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the regression line is

$$
y=4.7x+80.8.
$$

Finally, we can predict the height of a six-year-old child in this family by substituting $x=6$ into our regression line:

$$
y=4.7(6)+80.8=109
$$

Therefore, the model predicts that a six-year-old child will be $109.0\,\text{cm}$ tall.
